About

I am currently a Postdoctoral (FARE) Fellow in the Department of Earth Sciences at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, having submitted my Ph.D. thesis. My academic background is in geological sciences, with specialized expertise in palaeomagnetism, rock magnetism, and impact cratering.

My research focuses on the magnetic response of impactites and target rocks from the Dhala Impact Structure, India, with broader implications for planetary magnetism. I combine laboratory-based magnetic measurements, mineralogical characterization, and field-based geological investigations to understand how impact processes modify magnetic minerals and remanent magnetization.

PhD thesis · submitted
Effects of shock waves on magnetic properties of crystalline rocks: A case study from the Dhala Impact Structure, IndiaAdvisor: Dr. Amar Agarwal, Associate Professor, Department of Earth Sciences, IIT Kanpur

Research

Paleomagnetism

Investigation of remanent magnetization and paleomagnetic directions preserved in target rocks and impactites.

Rock magnetism

Characterization of magnetic minerals and their response to shock, thermal and geological processes.

Impact cratering

Magnetic and structural evidence for impact-related deformation, impact direction and subsurface impact-melt deposits.

Shock effects

Understanding shock-induced demagnetization and changes in magnetic properties of crystalline target rocks.

Planetary magnetism

Exploring implications of impact-related magnetic records for planetary magnetic-field evolution.

Field & laboratory integration

Combining field-based geological investigations with laboratory magnetometry, XRD and magnetic data analysis.
